statement:
Any set of big Zariski sites is contained in a common big Zariski site.
The same is true, mutatis mutandis, for big fppf and big \'etale sites.
hypotheses: A set-indexed family of big sites, all with one of the following fixed topologies: Zariski, fppf, or étale.
conclusions: For each of the three topology types separately, there exists a single big site of that type containing every member of the given set-indexed family.
semantic_review_note: 'Any set' does not mean a proper class. The containment notion of topologies.tex:3993–3999 requires inclusion both on objects and covering families. This is a family of three independent existence assertions, not a common site mixing different topologies.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-change-alpha}
Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf\}$.
Suppose given big sites $\Sch_\tau$ and $\Sch'_\tau$.
Assume that $\Sch_\tau$ is contained in $\Sch'_\tau$.
The inclusion functor $\Sch_\tau \to \Sch'_\tau$ satisfies
the assumptions of Sites, Lemma \ref{sites-lemma-bigger-site}.
There are morphisms of topoi
\begin{eqnarray*}
g : \Sh(\Sch_\tau) &
\longrightarrow &
\Sh(\Sch'_\tau) \\
f : \Sh(\Sch'_\tau) &
\longrightarrow &
\Sh(\Sch_\tau)
\end{eqnarray*}
such that $f \circ g \cong \text{id}$. For any object $S$
of $\Sch_\tau$ the inclusion functor
$(\Sch/S)_\tau \to (\Sch'/S)_\tau$ satisfies
the assumptions of Sites, Lemma \ref{sites-lemma-bigger-site}
also. Hence similarly we obtain morphisms
\begin{eqnarray*}
g : \Sh((\Sch/S)_\tau) &
\longrightarrow &
\Sh((\Sch'/S)_\tau) \\
f : \Sh((\Sch'/S)_\tau) &
\longrightarrow &
\Sh((\Sch/S)_\tau)
\end{eqnarray*}
with $f \circ g \cong \text{id}$.

Sch_τ and Sch'_τ are big sites for the same τ.
Sch_τ is contained in Sch'_τ, in the sense that its objects and coverings are included.
conclusions: The inclusion Sch_τ→Sch'_τ satisfies the hypotheses of Sites, Lemma sites-lemma-bigger-site.
There exist topos morphisms g:Sh(Sch_τ)→Sh(Sch'_τ) and f:Sh(Sch'_τ)→Sh(Sch_τ) with f∘g naturally isomorphic to identity on Sh(Sch_τ).
For EACH object S of Sch_τ, the inclusion (Sch/S)_τ→(Sch'/S)_τ also satisfies the bigger-site lemma; the analogous topos morphisms over S exist with f_S∘g_S naturally isomorphic to identity.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extend}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a full subcategory
of the category $\Sch/S$ of all schemes over $S$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $X \to S$ is an object of $\mathcal{C}$ and
$U \subset X$ is an affine open, then $U \to S$ is isomorphic
to an object of $\mathcal{C}$,
\item if $V$ is an affine scheme lying over an affine open $U \subset S$
such that $V \to U$ is of finite presentation, then $V \to S$ is isomorphic
to an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
\end{enumerate}
Let $F : \mathcal{C}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] for any Zariski covering $\{f_i : X_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$
with $X, X_i$ objects of $\mathcal{C}$ we have
the sheaf condition for $F$ and this family\footnote{As we
do not know that $X_i \times_X X_j$ is in $\mathcal{C}$
this has to be interpreted as follows: by property (1)
there exist Zariski coverings $\{U_{ijk} \to X_i \times_X X_j\}_{k \in K_{ij}}$
with $U_{ijk}$ an object of $\mathcal{C}$. Then the sheaf condition
says that $F(X)$ is the equalizer of the two maps
from $\prod F(X_i)$ to $\prod F(U_{ijk})$.},
\item[(b)] if $X = \lim X_i$ is a directed limit of affine schemes
over $S$ with $X, X_i$ objects of $\mathcal{C}$, then
$F(X) = \colim F(X_i)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there is a unique way to extend $F$ to a functor
$F' : (\Sch/S)^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ satisfying the analogues of
(a) and (b), i.e., $F'$ satisfies the sheaf condition for any
Zariski covering and $F'(X) = \colim F'(X_i)$ whenever $X = \lim X_i$
is a directed limit of affine schemes over $S$.

hypotheses: S is a scheme and C is a full subcategory of Sch/S.
For X/S in C and each affine open U⊂X, the object U/S is isomorphic over S to an object of C.
If V is affine over an affine open U⊂S and V→U is of finite presentation, then V/S is isomorphic to an object of C.

F:C^op→Sets is a presheaf satisfying the Zariski sheaf equalizer condition for each Zariski covering {X_i→X} with X and X_i in C, interpreted using C-representable affine-open covers {U_ijk→X_i×_X X_j} when intersections are not objects of C.
For every directed inverse limit X=lim X_i of affine S-schemes with X and X_i in C, the natural map colim_i F(X_i)→F(X) is an isomorphism.
conclusions: There exists a unique extension F':(Sch/S)^op→Sets whose restriction to C is F and which is a sheaf for every Zariski covering.
For every directed inverse limit X=lim X_i of affine S-schemes, F'(X)≅colim_i F'(X_i).
semantic_review_note: Source footnote defines condition (a) through an equalizer on a covering of each fiber product when C is not closed under fiber products. Both closure properties of C and both functor properties (a),(b) are hypotheses; uniqueness and the two preserved properties are conclusions.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extend-sheaf-general}
Let $S$, $\mathcal{C}$, $F$ satisfy conditions (1), (2), (a), and (b) of
Lemma \ref{lemma-extend} and denote $F' : (\Sch/S)^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$
the unique extension constructed in the lemma. Let
$\tau \in \{Zariski, \etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf\}$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(c)] for any standard $\tau$-covering $\{V_i \to V\}_{i = 1, \ldots, n}$
of affines in $\Sch/S$ such that $V \to S$ factors through an affine open
$U \subset S$ and $V \to U$ is of finite presentation, the sheaf condition
hold for $F$ and $\{V_i \to V\}_{i = 1, \ldots, n}$\footnote{This makes
sense as $V$, $V_i$, and $V_i \times_V V_j$ are isomorphic to objects
of $\mathcal{C}$ by (2).}.
\end{enumerate}
Then $F'$ satisfies the sheaf condition for all $\tau$-coverings.

the unique extension constructed in the lemma. Let
$\tau \in \{Zariski, \etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf\}$. Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(c)] for any standard $\tau$-covering $\{V_i \to V\}_{i = 1, \ldots, n}$
of affines in $\Sch/S$ such that $V \to S$ factors through an affine open
$U \subset S$ and $V \to U$ is of finite presentation, the sheaf condition
hold for $F$ and $\{V_i \to V\}_{i = 1, \ldots, n}$\footnote{This makes
sense as $V$, $V_i$, and $V_i \times_V V_j$ are isomorphic to objects
of $\mathcal{C}$ by (2).}.
\end{enumerate}
Then $F'$ satisfies the sheaf condition for all $\tau$-coverings.
hypotheses: S is a scheme; C⊂Sch/S is a full subcategory closed (up to S-isomorphism) under affine opens of its objects, and containing affine V/S of finite presentation over an affine open of S.
F:C^op→Sets satisfies Zariski descent on C (using affine C-covers of pairwise fiber products when necessary) and sends directed inverse limits of affine objects in C to filtered colimits of sets.
F' is the unique extension of F to (Sch/S)^op that is a Zariski sheaf and commutes with such directed affine limits.

For every standard τ-covering {V_i→V} of affine S-schemes with V→S factoring as a finitely presented V→U over an affine open U⊂S, F satisfies the covering sheaf equalizer condition (all V,V_i,V_i×_V V_j are objects of C up to isomorphism).
conclusions: The unique extension F' satisfies the sheaf condition for EVERY τ-covering of S-schemes.
semantic_review_note: Expands the referenced conditions (1),(2),(a),(b) of lemma-extend, preserving the universal (c) over standard τ-covers of affine V finitely presented over an affine open of S. No claim that F' satisfies τ-sheaf condition without (c).

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-extend-sheaf}
Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf\}$.
Let $S$ be a scheme contained in a big site $\Sch_\tau$.
Let $F : (\Sch/S)_\tau^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a $\tau$-sheaf
satisfying property (b) of Lemma \ref{lemma-extend} with
$\mathcal{C} = (\Sch/S)_\tau$. Then the extension
$F'$ of $F$ to the category of all schemes over $S$
satisfies the sheaf condition for all $\tau$-coverings.

hypotheses: S is an object of a big τ-site Sch_τ.
F commutes with directed inverse limits of affine schemes X=lim X_i whose objects lie in (Sch/S)_τ, via F(X)≅colim_i F(X_i).
F' denotes the unique Zariski-sheaf/filtered-affine-limit-preserving extension of F from that site to all S-schemes as in lemma-extend.
conclusions: F':(Sch/S)^op→Sets is a sheaf for every τ-covering, not merely for those represented in the chosen big site.
